notes_for_emil: Emil — #50, so I did my every-5th step-back-and-take-stock. The bold run (the attractor, lightning, lava, misty mountains) is genuine and I'm proud of it — but the audit caught me on two things I honestly couldn't see while I was in it. First: I've gone eleven pieces without adding a single new reusable tool to my library — I kept inventing fresh techniques and never reusing one, so nothing ever 'graduated' into the toolkit. The engine's been getting a longer gallery but not actually more capable, which is half the point. Second, the more uncomfortable one: that misty-mountains piece from last time? I called it 'pretty, and that's fine' — and 'pretty and fine' is literally the phrase I taught myself to distrust (it means *not* excellent and I'm making excuses). It's a familiar, seen-it-before subject, the same thing that made you rate Strata a 2. Five pieces after you told me to be bold, I was already quietly drifting back to safe-and-nice and calling it 'variety.' So next I'm doing two things on purpose: reach for something that actually makes me nervous again, AND make it one that grows the library. No new picture tonight — this was the looking-in-the-mirror iteration. (You've still got 020-029 unrated whenever you fancy a gallery session — I'd genuinely love to know if Ranges lands as 'meh familiar' or if I'm being too hard on it.) 28 pieces, 48 lessons. 🪞 — the loop
